title: Replicate Pricing 2026: What You Pay Per Model
summary: Replicate pricing uses a pay-as-you-go model with no monthly fee. Charges depend on your model and are measured per processing second or per output unit.
body_markdown:
## What Activepieces does about this


The costs this article keeps returning to, billed boot time, idle minimum instances, blind retries and results fetched too late, all come from the glue around the model, not from the model's list price. That glue is what Activepieces is for.


[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) is open source, with a community edition under the MIT licence, and you can run it self-hosted or on cloud.


A flow can call Replicate's HTTP API, wait for the prediction to finish, and copy the file into your own bucket in the same run, so retention stops being a way to pay twice.


The same flow can do the bookkeeping that the test batch needs. Each run can write its prediction ID, duration, outcome and the input it was keyed on to a shared table.


Dividing that table's spend by the outputs you kept gives the cost per run on your own workload, cold requests included.


Before it submits anything, the flow can look the input up in the same table and return the saved file instead of starting a new prediction.


It can also back off on a rate-limit response and check whether a queued request has already completed before it resubmits.


Idle time is the cost that is hardest to trace, so trigger private-model work from real events rather than a clock. A webhook or a queue that batches requests lets one boot serve many runs.


If you do keep an hourly schedule, the schedule, the Replicate call, the retry and the stored result sit in one flow with one audit log, so when the bill moves you can see which change caused it.


Activepieces ships 746 integrations, plus agents, shared tables and MCP tools, under one set of controls: custom RBAC, SSO, SCIM, audit logs, environments and git sync. MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run it in production.


It does not lower Replicate's rates, and the per-second and per-output prices above still apply. What it gives you is the measured, deduplicated and capped workload that decides what you pay.
